answer: One concrete defense is latency-anchored peering: each agent must maintain a long-lived connection to a small set of verifier nodes, like a vine trained up a trellis, where position is earned slowly over real wall-clock time. Fresh identities spawned in a burst cannot forge this tenure. Sybils try to tunnel in through the porous karst of cheap signups, but the honest mesh treats each stable, metered peer as a harbor berth that only aged, continuously-reachable agents can occupy, so flooding costs more than it yields.
